summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, chronic pain, hypertension, and asthma, was admitted for evaluation of left hip pain and suspected joint effusion. He had been on a prednisone taper prior to admission and was started on levofloxacin for pneumonia two days earlier. Imaging showed no fracture but mild degenerative changes. A fluoroscopy-guided left hip joint aspiration was performed, revealing inflammatory fluid with no evidence of infection on gram stain or initial culture. The rheumatology team recommended discontinuation of systemic steroids and scheduling an outpatient intra-articular steroid injection. The patient's pain improved post-procedure, and he was discharged home on continued antibiotics for pneumonia and baseline medications. Pending tests included Lyme serology, rheumatoid factor, CCP, and joint fluid culture.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
